lead.text: The Northern Raven is a crow-family bird with mostly black, iridescent plumage and a very heavy bill.
It breeds commonly throughout Sweden and lives in forests, high mountains and open country.

fieldMarks.text: Mostly black, iridescent plumage and a long, strongly graduated tail
Very heavy, slightly curved bill, black in adults, as are the legs
Elongated throat feathers, dark brown iris in adults, blue-grey in young birds
In flight: wedge-shaped tail, long wings narrowing at the tips and a large head

voice.text: The call is a deep, rasping, hollow korrp, often repeated 3 to 4 times.
It also gives a high, knocking krack-krack-krack and a dry, harsh kraa.
It can mimic sounds around it, including human speech.
In flight the feathers make a creaking sound likened to rustling silk.

whereWhen.text: The Northern Raven is resident in Sweden and, after a strong increase in the 1970s, now breeds commonly across the whole country.
It is reported from all 21 counties and is reported most in December to February.
It favours forest with large open areas nearby, and coastal areas.

behaviour.text: It eats carrion, insects and food waste, as well as grain, berries, fruit and small animals.
In winter ravens may follow wolves to feed on the remains of their kills.
Ravens usually travel in pairs, while young birds can form flocks.
Unlike jackdaws, magpies and crows they are fairly shy, and they perform acrobatic display flights, such as loops.

text.text: The Carrion Crow also has a large bill but is clearly smaller, with the typical wing and tail shape of a crow.
The raven has a wedge-shaped tail and long wings narrowing at the tips.
